ledger.why: the casting line (the roles carry it)

collection.description: A villager ties a knot in a long string after every really good day, and a friend finds it while tidying.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) keeps a long piece of string in (subject.his/her) hut. Whenever (subject.he/she) has a good day, a really good one, (subject.he/she) ties a knot in it. It's been going for many years. The string is now so long it has to be wound up like a ball of fishing line. (friend) finds it while helping to tidy and asks what it is.

a.name: Answer A
a.text: They sit down and start counting. Some knots (subject) remembers perfectly: the day of the big catch, the day the roof didn't leak. Some (subject.he/she) can't remember at all, and that's somehow nice too. They lose count somewhere past two hundred and start laughing. (subject) ties one more knot before (friend) leaves.

b.name: Answer B
b.text: (subject) cuts a short piece of string from the end and hands it over. "For your good days," (subject.he/she) says. (friend) looks at the empty string, puzzled. That evening the fishing goes well, dinner is excellent, and (friend) quietly ties a knot in it before bed.
